summary_en: This Phase 2 trial tests durvalumab given with chemotherapy in patients with locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors. Durvalumab is given into a vein with one of several chemotherapy drugs, in cycles of 21 or 28 days that repeat while the disease does not progress and side effects are not unacceptable. The official title says the study evaluates safety and pharmacodynamics, and a primary outcome measure is not stated.
summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 2 evalúa durvalumab administrado junto con quimioterapia en pacientes con tumores sólidos localmente avanzados o metastásicos. Durvalumab se administra por vena junto con uno de varios medicamentos de quimioterapia, en ciclos de 21 o 28 días que se repiten mientras la enfermedad no progrese y los efectos secundarios no sean inaceptables. El título oficial indica que el estudio evalúa la seguridad y la farmacodinamia, y no se indica una medida de resultado principal.
who_for: Metastatic or locally advanced solid tumor that progressed after at least one line of standard therapy.
Tumor that can be biopsied, and willingness to undergo a biopsy.
Age 18 or older, with ECOG performance status of 2 or less.
Adequate blood counts, liver function and kidney function, as defined in the criteria.
not_for: Prior checkpoint inhibitor stopped because of a serious adverse event.
Pancreatic, prostate, or MSS colorectal cancer: durvalumab alone is not given, but chemotherapy combinations are allowed.
